defectsCP2CaughtInThisLanesOwnWork.defect: THE EDGE WAS NOT WHERE THE DISPATCH SAID THE EDGE WAS, and shipping the obvious fix would have changed nothing that was MEASURED.
defectsCP2CaughtInThisLanesOwnWork.howItShowedUp: The dispatch cites `src/jobs/bastrop-publish.mjs` and says 'the caller that reaches the job's top level prints only the code'. That is true of the file's own `if (process.argv[1]?.endsWith('bastrop-publish.mjs'))` block -- and that block NEVER RUNS in the deployed job. Dockerfile.publish's `ENTRYPOINT ["node", "src/cli.mjs"]` plus cloudbuild.publish.yaml's `--command=node,src/cli.mjs --args=bastrop-publish,...` mean the 11-entry log came from src/cli.mjs's `main().catch`. The job's block is only reached when the file is invoked directly, which nothing on Cloud Run does.
defectsCP2CaughtInThisLanesOwnWork.theFix: src/cli.mjs's catch prints the bounded form. The job's own block was fixed too (it is the right shape for a direct invocation and costs one line), but the deployed edge is the one that matters.
defectsCP2CaughtInThisLanesOwnWork.whyItIsRecorded: A lane that had fixed only the job would have opened a PR, passed tests, and left the measured symptom (`BAKE_FAILED` as the only log line) exactly as it was -- a control that cannot fire. The reading that caught it was the deployment wiring, not the job source, which is the general lesson: 'the caller that prints it' must be read from the entrypoint, never from the file the dispatch points at.

defectsCP2CaughtInThisLanesOwnWork.howItShowedUp: The naming rule's bare form requires the WHOLE line to be SCREAMING_SNAKE, so a 5MB line of `A_B_C_...` matched and was returned as the refusal name. That name lands in `runs.refuse_code` (a `text` column, no length limit) and in every log line -- the same unbounded-at-rest defect the row exists to close, reintroduced through the name instead of the tail. defectsCP2CaughtInThisLanesOwnWork.theFix: `MAX_REFUSAL_NAME_CHARS = 96`. A token longer than that is a payload, not a name; its tail still carries it verbatim and the failure is named BAKE_FAILED, which is the honest answer. Asserted in both directions (200-char token -> null; 96-char token -> the name).

honestLimits: The record carries a TAIL. 8192 bytes and 40 lines of each stream, the end of it. A refusal whose words appear EARLIER than the last 40 lines of a very chatty child is not in the record. The name is read from the RAW stream before bounding, so the name survives a chatty child; the measurement text around it may not.

The name is read ONLY from the last non-empty line. The bake CLIs put their refusal there (they print it and exit), so this is the strongest available signal and not a placeholder -- but a child that prints its code and then another log line afterwards is NOT named, and the tail is then the whole of the record. Stated in the module header as a contract rather than left as an accident.

A single-word code (no underscore) is NOT named, deliberately: `ERROR` and `WARNING` would otherwise become refusal names, and a wrong name is worse than none. The cost is refused precision on `refuse_code`, never the words.

The bound protects the RECORD and the LOG line. It does not bound what `execFile` buffers in memory before the failure (the call sites allow 20MB); a child that prints more than that fails with ERR_CHILD_PROCESS_STDIO_MAXBUFFER, which this module keeps as the errno (failing to RUN is a different fact from refusing) and records with whatever partial output the error carries.
The `run_events` row is one row per failure. A publish that retries and fails twice writes two rows -- there is no de-duplication and none was added, because each failure is its own event.

publish-gate-sched.mjs's gate-CLI path and cloudrun-jobs.mjs's gcloud calls are NAMED as out of scope in CP1, not fixed. A gate refusals' words still live only in the process; that is a different surface's row.
whatWouldFalsifyThisLane: If a real bake refusal after this lands still leaves `refuse_code = BAKE_FAILED` on the run row when the child printed a named refusal, the naming rule is wrong about what the child prints and must be re-derived from the child's source rather than adjusted by taste.

If Cloud Logging after a real failure shows the log line WITHOUT the tails, then the deployed entrypoint is not src/cli.mjs for that job (it is for factory-bastrop-publish and factory-dollar-fields-patch per cloudbuild.publish.yaml, read at d1b6ea07) and the edge assumption is wrong for it.

If a run_events row of kind `subprocess-refusal` cannot be written for any legitimate reason and the run's failure path then behaves differently from before, the catch that reports-loudly-rather-than-throws is the wrong trade and must be re-decided with the store's error in hand.
If a nameless failure stops being recorded (a regression to the old shape), F2 fails; if a REFUSAL loses its tail because the child's output exceeded 20MB, the partial-output arm is the one to read.
